speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The shooting pain when eating suggests possible trismus or referred pain from the masseter muscle, which is a known complication after tympanoplasty. Given your history of chronic ear infections and the specific nature of the pain, could you describe if the pain radiates to your jaw or if you have noticed any difficulty opening your mouth fully? Also, have you noticed any discharge or fluid leaking from the right ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (post-tympanoplasty) secondary to Frey's Syndrome, complicated by trismus.
